text:
oncall-bot: PAGER DUTY — P1: Elevated SRV/DNS lookup errors in us-west2 (detected at 2026-03-15T18:28Z). Affects internal service discovery and edge-proxy route selection. Pager -> @alyssa. Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/dns-srv

alyssa: Im awake, taking this. Starting with metrics and coredns logs.

alyssa: grafana: coredns SERVFAIL rate spiking from ~0.2% -> ~35% in us-west2a around 18:24Z. latency for rcode=NXDOMAIN up too.

matt: also seeing increased 5xx from edge-proxy to backend-orchestrator. Correlates to SRV resolution timeouts.

sara: tagging this as P1 for now. Alyssa, if coredns is unhealthy, can we scale or restart while we triage?

alyssa: plan: 1) roll coredns in us-west2a 2) scale replicas 3) enable edge-proxy fallback to remote DC 4) monitor. Executing step 1 now.

alyssa: ```
kubectl -n kube-system scale deployment/coredns --replicas=6
kubectl -n kube-system rollout restart deployment/coredns
```

ops-bot: deploy-bot: rollout restart started for deployment/coredns (kube-system) by alyssa at 18:31Z.

infra-bot: cloud-health: detected increased packet loss on us-west2a internal fabric peers between control-plane and worker subnets during 18:20-18:35Z. Possible AZ routing flap.

matt: if control-plane->coredns queries get dropped, you'll see SERVFAIL and high retransmits. Confirming that from tcpdump on kube-dns node: many retransmits to 169.254.x.x (provider metadata) and timeouts.

alyssa: scaling seemed to help a bit, SERVFAIL dropped to ~12% after pods came up. But still intermittent.

jim: On edge-proxy I can enable SRV cache TTL to reduce lookup pressure. Quick toggle config: EDGE_SRV_CACHE_TTL=30s. Pushing to staging first.

alyssa: please push, jim. Also enabling fallback routing so proxies can prefer us-west1 while us-west2 heals.

jim: ```
# curl to admin API
curl -X POST https://edge-admin.internal/config -d '{"edge": {"srv_cache_ttl": "30s", "prefer_remote_dc": true}}'
```

ops-bot: config-change: edge-proxy config updated (who=jim, change=edge.srv_cache_ttl,true) at 18:36Z.

sara: Quick customer impact notes: internal background ingestion jobs and some inter-service RPCs are failing intermittently. External API endpoints show normal behavior for most customers, but a few internal integrations reporting delayed processing. Estimated affected workload: ~12% of internal requests; no external SLA breach at this time. Notifying CS for customers with Dedicated/private placements in us-west2.

alyssa: digging deeper into cloud provider: theres an ongoing network maintenance event in us-west2a that appears to have triggered route withdrawal, causing controller plane connectivity blips. Filed ticket with provider: INC-45321.

matt: mitigation if provider issue persists: pin coredns to other AZs, force pod anti-affinity to get replicas into us-west2b/c and us-west1. Also add iptables conntrack tweak on nodes to reduce ephemeral NAT exhaustion.

alyssa: running conntrack tweak on a small set of nodes: ```
sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=524288
sysctl -w net.ipv4.netfilter.ip_conntrack_max=524288
```

alyssa: rolling coredns pods off the problematic AZ (force schedule) now.

matt: Im taking over the page from alyssa for the next 30m (handoff). @alyssa, thanks. Ill coordinate with provider and infra.

alyssa: thx, matt — leaving notes in runbook and switching to standby.

matt: provider support says they saw a routing mesh reconvergence that dropped control-plane packets for ~7m; theyre rolling a fix. They recommend keeping traffic routed away from us-west2a for 30m and throttling SRV resolution pressure.

matt: current status: coredns SERVFAIL ~3-7% (steady), edge-proxy fallback active, SRV cache enabled. Traffic routed away from us-west2a by smart-router.

sara: ACTIONS: create postmortem (owner=matt), followup to CS (owner=sara), update runbook with provider routing steps (owner=alyssa).

infra-bot: incident-bot: paging reminder: if error rate >10% for 15m escalate to oncall lead.

matt: monitoring shows error rate back under threshold for 10m now. Im going to scale down coredns back to usual and keep fallback rules in place until provider confirms stable.

ops-bot: rollout complete: deployment/coredns scaled back to 3 replicas at 18:55Z.

matt: provider confirms routing fix applied at 18:50Z. We will keep an eye for 1h.

sara: Customer impact summary for postmortem: intermittent SRV lookup failures caused ~12% internal request degradation, limited customer-facing impact. No data loss, retries handled. CS notified for targeted customers.

matt: RESOLVED: root cause: cloud-provider AZ routing reconvergence causing control-plane packet loss -> coredns query timeouts; mitigation: scaled coredns, enabled SRV caching, routed traffic away from problematic AZ, conntrack tuning. Postmortem will be filed by EOD. Closing page in 1h if stable. :white_check_mark:

ops-bot: incident-note: ticket INC-45321 opened with provider. Postmortem draft ticket created: PM-7721.

sara: thanks everyone — great coordination.

matt: handing back to alyssa for any additional notes.

alyssa: all good, Ill add notes to the runbook and leave followups.

oncall-bot: This thread will be archived to incidents after 2 hours.
